text:
AI can make it almost free to create economic agents.

That means one actor could create thousands of bots to spam transactions, compete for ordering, or manipulate markets etc. at very low cost in many systems. 

PoW creates a different constraint identities are cheap, but meaningful economic influence still requires real world resources.

AI makes participation abundant. 

PoW keeps influence scarce.

Pow derived economic ordering enforces this sybil constraint in other layers. 

Which probably will be a good thing as AI adoption accelerates.

title: Proof of "I'm human" will become the foundation for agents, dating, lending and gating. But the authors of the paper on personhood credentia
text:
Proof of "I'm human" will become the foundation for agents, dating, lending and gating. But the authors of the paper on personhood credentials name 4 risks:

1. Who the system will leave without access

If the barriers created by PHCs are too high, some users may stop using them and thus miss out on the privacy benefits they provide.

2. Will people speak freely under "verification"

It is important to consider how PHCs may reduce people's willingness to speak freely and express dissent online. People may fear that their online statements will be linked to their real-world identity, even if PHCs do not reveal who they are.

3. Who will get power over issuing proofs

One of the significant problems of the PHC ecosystem is the concentration of power in the hands of a small number of institutions. User information is one potential source of power for the issuer.

4. How it will be broken and where it will make mistakes

A PHC system, like any digital system, is vulnerable to attacks and exploits from many actors, first and foremost subversion by the issuer itself, service providers and malicious users.

title: Over 50% of transactions on Solana today are failed arbitrage bots spamming the network for a chance at MEV.  They're not "wrong" to do it
text:
Over 50% of transactions on Solana today are failed arbitrage bots spamming the network for a chance at MEV.

They're not "wrong" to do it  with fees this low, spamming positive-EV trades pays off over time, even with a majority failure rate. But it means half of Solana's throughput is bots retrying, not humans transacting.

Jito alone has distributed over 4.3M SOL in MEV rewards since launch, proof of how much value is being fought over in that spam.

Raiku's JIT lets searchers bid for bundle execution directly instead of flooding the mempool with retries  MEV capture without the network-wide spam tax.

title: AI TRUST How Can AI Agents Trust Each Other?  If AI Agents can buy and sell services, one question becomes critical:  How can they trust eac
text:
AI TRUST
How Can AI Agents Trust Each Other?

If AI Agents can buy and sell services,
one question becomes critical:

How can they trust each other?

An AI Agent needs to know:

Who are you?
What can you do?
Can I verify your results?
Can I trust your transaction history?

This creates a new layer:

AI Trust.

The basic model could be:

Identity → Credentials → Reputation → Verification → Transaction.

Blockchain can record verifiable actions.

Digital identity can identify the agent.

Smart contracts can enforce agreed rules.

And reputation can provide evidence of past performance.

InterLink's direction around Proof of Personhood, InterLink ID, blockchain infrastructure, and digital commerce provides building blocks for a human-centered trust layer in an AI-driven ecosystem.

But technology alone cannot guarantee that an AI is trustworthy.

Trust must be verifiable.

In the human economy,
we ask:

“Who are you?”

In the AI economy,
we may also ask:

“What has your AI done before?”
